clue.text: Music's provided by Soft Cell singer, mostly: something fishy about this

parts.note: rock is a genre of music, here with its possessive S

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Marc Almond fronted the 1980s synth-pop duo Soft Cell

explanation.surface: A tribute to rock music and an eighties pop singer, with something suspicious lurking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ALMOND to ALMON. 'Soft' looks like an anagram signal or an S, but Soft Cell is the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish, so it is literally a fish.

clue.text: Registered companies adopting circular style of architecture

indicators.note: adopting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for registered, as in a trademark
CO is short for company, so two COs stand for companies
a circular shape is a ring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Registered firms take up a round-fronted building style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts O after R, between R and COCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century decorative style that followed Baroque.

clue.text: It can be seen from Dover station

definitions.text: It can be seen from Dover
definitions.meaning: the stretch of sea between England and France lies in view of Dover's cliffs
a television station is a broadcasting outlet

explanation.surface: A view from Dover, or Dover's railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Channel is visible from Dover, and a TV channel is a broadcasting station.

clue.text: Males do misbehave repetitively: that's nothing new

indicators.note: repetitively tells us to give the result twice over
misbehave suggests the letters behave badly and get jumbled

explanation.surface: Men keep behaving badly, again and again: nothing surprising there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehave' rearranges MALESDO into SAMEOLD, and 'repetitively' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for tiresome routine, nothing fresh or different.

clue.text: English newspaper with items about recycled food

explanation.surface: An English paper runs pieces about food that is used again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items' looks like newspaper articles, but here it means couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneaten portions saved and served again at a later meal are reused food.

clue.text: Indian version of duck with herb

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the letter O
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: An Indian take on a duck-and-herb dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' is a link here. A duck is a batter's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Slowly drink about a litre and lose balance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drink goes round the litre

parts.note: to sip is to drink slowly

explanation.surface: Someone sips a litre and ends up unsteady on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to lose footing and stumble.

clue.text: Amorous meetings I noted in racy novels

indicators.note: racy suggests lively, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Romantic encounters, as I've spotted in steamy fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted in' is a link: the I joins the letters of NOVELS, and 'racy' shuffles all seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-ins were 1960s hippie gatherings celebrating love and peace.

clue.text: Perfect location is within AUROR row of shops

indicators.note: within places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a parade is a row of shops in British usage

explanation.surface: An ideal spot sits inside a shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: A parade in Britain is a row of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a place of perfect happiness, an ideal setting.

clue.text: Picture flipping team and reserve as well

definitions.text: Picture flipping team and reserve as well

parts.words: Picture flipping team and reserve as well
parts.note: picture means film; flipping means cross; a cricket or football team of eleven plus a reserve makes a dozen players

explanation.surface: A photo of a team turning over, with its substitute too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like turning over, but means annoyed; eleven players plus a reserve make twelve men.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1957 courtroom drama film is about a jury of a dozen men arguing, a group of jurors fitting the clue.

clue.text: Daily Mirror leader's appeal

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner, also called a char or charwoman

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The front page of a tabloid newspaper makes a plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Mirror' looks like the newspaper; 'Daily' is a cleaning lady (a char) and the Mirror gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm and appeal are synonyms for attractiveness.

clue.text: Patriotic type seen to falter, then hesitate

parts.note: to flag is to tire or falter
to waver is to hesitate

explanation.surface: A patriot is seen to weaken and then dither.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag-waver is someone who loudly displays national pride.

clue.text: Sadly for a musician, learning's complex to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the complex at the start of the answer

parts.note: a condo is a block or complex of flats
lore is learning or traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Unhappily, a musician finds learning complicated at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like an adjective or anagram signal but is a noun: a condominium block.
explanation.definitionFit: Con dolore is an Italian musical direction meaning play with sorrow.

clue.text: Landowner, one wearing flashy clothes and diamonds

parts.note: in Australian slang a lair is a showily dressed man
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A landowner dressed in gaudy clothes and jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIR is Australian slang for a show-off in loud clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Us city encounters troubles importing oriental orchids

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a US city

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: distresses means troubles
E stands for east, hence oriental

explanation.surface: An American city faces problems bringing in flowers from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' puts E inside DISTRESSES after the I; 'encounters' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies' tresses are a genus of small orchids with spiralled flower spikes.

clue.text: Kurd hates disentangling knot

indicators.note: disentangling suggests untangling and rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A Kurdish man despises undoing knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disentangling' looks part of the scene with knots but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turk's head is a decorative sailor's knot woven like a turban.

clue.text: Soldier in a pub not UINI SIP D making any sense

definitions.text: not UINI SIP D making any sense

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the pub

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a pub talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British word for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Alogical means outside or opposed to logic, without reason.

clue.text: Long-term policy needed as final rescue fails

indicators.note: fails suggests a breakdown, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-standing plan is required as a last-ditch rescue collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Life assurance is an insurance policy paying out on death, held for many years.

clue.text: Men in a state of Y K agitation a very long time

indicators.note: in places the men inside the agitation

parts.words: a state of Y K agitation
parts.note: fever is a state of nervous excitement
OR means other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Men kept in a nervous state for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever is an informal word for an extremely long period.

clue.text: Theologian certain to get worked up about a saint

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the rest
worked up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A theologian sure to become agitated about a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked up' turns SURE to ERUS, and 'about' puts it around AST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Erastus was a sixteenth-century Swiss physician and religious thinker.

clue.text: Woman housed in hostel lately

clue.text: Wolf in ravine

a ravine is a deep narrow valley

explanation.surface: A wolf lurking in a deep valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorge means both to eat greedily and a steep-sided valley.

clue.text: Watchful old boy prepared to protect rare vehicle

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to protect means enclosing, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
a van is a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: Observant means alert and quick to notice things.

clue.text: Shout of joy heralding Black American, top-grade president

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession, originally of riders.

clue.text: Accommodation in remote land

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of the clue words

explanation.surface: Lodging in a faraway country.

clue.text: Early bird's foolish activity

definitions.meaning: someone who rises early is called a ..., after the songbird

explanation.surface: An early riser gets up to some silly business.
explanation.definitionFit: The songbird sings at dawn and gives its name to early risers; a lark is also a prank.

clue.text: Revolutionary soldiers on beach in island

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of
